own_summary.heading: Summary of investigations and key findings

sentences.text: IBAC reported on corruption in Victorian prisons through four investigations: Operations Rous, Caparra, Nisidia and Molara.
sentences.support: This report focuses on four investigations – Operations Rous, Caparra, Nisidia and Molara

sentences.text: It examined conduct in public and private prisons, including assaults, information misuse, undisclosed associations and tobacco smuggling.
sentences.support: including excessive use of force, masking behaviours, misuse of information, inappropriate relationships and trafficking of contraband

sentences.text: IBAC found excessive force and failures in incident reporting at Port Phillip Prison, and identified improper relationships, information access and payments for tobacco smuggling in other investigations.
sentences.support: IBAC found corrections staff at Loddon and Dhurringile Prisons corruptly received cash payments to smuggle tobacco

sentences.text: It made three additional recommendations on prison controls and training, a statutory duty to report suspected corruption and a culture that supports reporting.
sentences.support: introduce a statutory obligation on corrections officers to report to the prison governor or to IBAC

findings.quote: In Operation Rous, IBAC found that certain corrections officers at Port Phillip Prison had used excessive force against two prisoners, one of whom has an intellectual disability.
In Operations Nisidia and Molara, IBAC found corrections staff at Loddon and Dhurringile Prisons corruptly received cash payments to smuggle tobacco into the facilities.

notes: Three is the count of additional numbered recommendations in this special report. Findings are stated separately from criminal prosecution outcomes and from unsubstantiated allegations.
